newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Abecafe awaits govt request on coffee sales.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Abecafe awaits govt request on coffee sales.

text.p: Brazil's Coffee Exporters' Association (Abecafe) has not officially received any request from the gvernment to make no further sales for June shipment or delay June shipments if possible to July, the Abecafe head said.

Earlier today, top government commodity official Mauricio Assis requested the cooperation of exporters at a meeting with officials from the Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Federation (Febec), traditionally Brazil's key exporters' body.
"The government has to make this request officially to Abecafe. I do not recognise it through Febec," said Jorge Esteve, Abecafe president.
The government made the request after evaluating current export performance in the light of a limit agreed with members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC).

Under the accord, Brazil should ship no more than six million bags between January and June this year. But unofficial figures show that Brazilian coffee exports have already exceeded the six million bag limit by the end of May.

Assis declined to estimate what will be January to June exports but other exporting officials have said they now expect total July 1996 to June 1997 shipments to surpass Brazil's 15 million bag allowance by around 1.2 million bags. ((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
